decisive_moments.reason: Pro directly addressed the strongest objection by distinguishing preregistration from a fixed one-shot plan and proposing amendments, adaptive sampling, proportionate templates, and exemptions.

Con correctly identified the unresolved incentive problem: documentation and amendment costs may fall disproportionately on iterative, low-resource exploratory researchers, and labeling work exploratory does not guarantee equal publication or funding rewards.

Pro made the clearest system-level epistemic case: timestamped histories and open data improve transparency but do not as reliably establish what was specified before outcomes, leaving prediction, discovery, and selective reporting harder to distinguish.
Con showed that the comparative burden was not fully demonstrated, especially regarding compliance, fair treatment of deviations, and whether reduced discovery could undermine later verification.

flags.quote: those costs are outweighed by more reliable cumulative knowledge
A proportionate default with amendments, exemptions, and low-cost templates preserves adaptive inquiry
individual rationality can shift toward safer, less adaptive projects, reducing the discoveries that verification later depends on
